title: KV cache compact encoding: INT4/INT8/FP8 fidelity & memory exploration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Evaluate compact encodings for the KV cache (INT4, INT8, FP8-style 8-bit floats) to reduce GPU memory footprint and improve batching headroom while measuring fidelity regressions across representative Redwood workloads. Scope: experiments cover encoding/packing layout, retrieval/deserialize cost, approximation error (logprob drift, token-level deltas), and interactions with continuous batching and prefix reuse caching. We will not change model weights or inference kernels beyond packing/unpacking; the runtime should be able to switch cache encoding at model-load or per-namespace. Success is defined quantitatively (see acceptance_criteria).
acceptance_criteria: Memory: At least 2x reduction vs baseline FP16 for at least one encoding with minimal runtime unpack overhead (<3% median latency regression at p50)

Quality: Token-level distribution shift <= 1.0% absolute for conversational/regeneration workloads (measured by delta token logprob and next-token argmax divergence), and end-to-end task accuracy/ROUGE/perp regressions within predefined thresholds for eval suites

Determinism: Encoded+decoded KV should reproduce identical deterministic outputs for inference modes where model RNG is fixed; small floating jitter allowed but must not change beam/argmax choices for >99% tokens
Operational: Runtime fallback to full-precision cache on drift detection or customer opt-out, and metrics/emitter hooks in Console to show encoding usage and quality regressions
plan: Phase 0: Implement packed KV layout and GPU-side unpack kernel skeletons: contiguous packing per attention head to optimize memcpy and coalescing
Phase 1: Small-scale accuracy sweep on a 7B and 13B public model snapshots: FP8 emulation, symmetric INT8, asymmetric INT4 with scaling/zero-point per-head and global scaling variants
Phase 2: Long-context stability tests (8k-64k tokens) with prefix reuse to see accumulation drift, and replay tests to ensure no catastrophic divergence on repeated cache reuse
Phase 3: Integrate with continuous batching path and measure end-to-end p50/p95 latency under production-like concurrency; measure GPU memory headroom and effective throughput gains
Phase 4: Run Redwood eval harness (recall/accuracy suites + prompt mixtures) and customer-simulated traffic scenarios; log token-delta distributions into Console dashboards
Phase 5: Gate review: safety and accuracy review with Applied ML and PM, followed by canary rollout on internal Dedicated pool and opt-in Beta for select customers
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off spike. Implemented initial packed layout in a branch and validated that contiguous per-head packing reduces memcpy calls by ~60% in microbenchmarks.

2026-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Pilot INT8 emulation run on 13B snapshot (fp16 baseline). Observed mean token_logprob_delta ~0.002 nat/token and next-token divergence 0.4% on short-context chat prompts. Memory down ~1.9x. Need long-context tests.
2026-02-24 - Review (Applied ML): Suggested per-head scaling rather than global scaling for INT4 to reduce large-head bias. Added set of adversarial prompts with repeating patterns for stress tests.

2026-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: FP8 emulation shows similar fidelity to INT8 on majority of suites but better stability on repeated prefixes; unpack kernel overhead ~1.8% p50 latency. INT4 aggressive variant shows ~3.6x memory reduction but token divergence spikes on long dependency traces (>=16k tokens).
2026-03-04 - PM Liaison (Sofia Chen): Added customer gating: require <0.5% user-visible task error increase for beta customers. Raised canary cohort for Dedicated pool to 5 internal teams.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Next steps added: finalize kernel fuse for unpack+attention load to shave unpack cost, and script automatic drift detector that flips cached segments back to FP16 if divergence threshold exceeded in production
open_questions: What per-head scaling granularity gives best trade-off: per-head, per-layer, or global?
Does mixed encoding (FP8 for keys, INT8 for values) deliver materially better downstream quality for little extra complexity?
How to represent zero-point and scale metadata compactly without increasing per-entry overhead?
Operational policy: automatic fallback thresholds vs. manual opt-out for enterprise customers
decision_log: 2026-02-20 - Decided to prioritize FP8 emulation and INT8 symmetric first, postpone aggressive INT4 variants until we have better per-head scaling heuristics
2026-03-03 - Decided to implement runtime quality emitter in Console showing per-deployment divergence metrics before any canary rollout
next_steps: Optimize unpack kernel: fuse unpack+attention gather to reduce memory traffic (assigned Marco)
Run 64k token long-run experiments for FP8 and INT8 on 13B and 70B snapshots (use internal Dedicated cluster)
Implement drift detector and on-the-fly fallback mechanism in runtime and add telemetry hooks to Console
Prepare a canary plan and customer communication template for beta opt-in
outcome_summary: In-progress: early pilots show FP8 and INT8 provide favorable memory/perf trade-offs with small fidelity deltas for short- and mid-length contexts. INT4 offers the largest memory savings but requires stronger per-head scaling and has instability on long-context replay. Technical work focuses on lowering unpack overhead and adding runtime safeguards for canary rollouts.
